clue.text: Book to accompany scorer's work?

parts.note: the scorer is not a sportsman but a composer writing a score, and the book is the text of words sung to it in an opera

explanation.surface: Someone keeping score at a match wants a notebook to go with the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests cricket or football; here it is the composer who scores an opera, and the 'book' is the opera's words.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera's libretto is traditionally called its book: the written words set to the composer's music.

clue.text: Graduate tax upset vote

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: A graduate tax that upset people is put to a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret vote cast on paper is a ballot.

clue.text: Part of book that wants reading, maybe, in bar

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the extract

parts.note: an excerpt is a passage extracted from a book
reading is one of the three Rs, so R stands for it

explanation.surface: Part of a book in need of reading is taken to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; 'maybe' marks reading as one example of R. 'in' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition, bar means apart from, as in all bar one.

clue.text: College car not in order for a modern politician?

parts.note: a tech is a technical college

indicators.note: the letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A college car is out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges CAR NOT to give NOCRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical expert in government is a modern sort of political figure, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Mark that's left in cliff

definitions.meaning: a lasting mark left on the skin after a wound heals
in northern English dialect a steep rocky outcrop or crag

explanation.surface: Someone spots a mark left behind in a cliff face.
explanation.definitionFit: A healed wound leaves a lasting blemish, and in northern place names the same word is a steep rocky crag.

clue.text: Lawsuit with French aristo turning to cross large street

indicators.note: the turned letters stretch across and around the size abbreviation
both pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit in court
a duc is a French duke
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes

explanation.surface: A French nobleman in a lawsuit turns across a big road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses CASEDUC to CUDESAC, which goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end road is a particular kind of street closed at one end.

clue.text: Hold back concerning muscle problem

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a strain is a muscle injury

explanation.surface: Someone holds back because of a pulled muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb or keep in check is to hold something back.

clue.text: Fellow taken with engraved work that's attractive

indicators.note: one piece placed alongside the other

parts.note: an etching is a print from an engraved plate

explanation.surface: A man is taken with an attractive engraving.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetching outfit is attractive, the word meaning charming to look at.

clue.text: Truffle, perhaps, from food shop, more or less cold, an unknown quantity

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop selling prepared foods
ca is the abbreviation of circa, meaning about or approximately
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps
in algebra Y is a conventional symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A truffle bought from a delicatessen, served cold and of uncertain weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A truffle is a prized rare food, an example of a gourmet treat; the question mark signals the example.

clue.text: Desperate character embracing wife in beginning

indicators.note: the character holds the letter inside, as in an embrace

parts.note: Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British children's comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A desperate man embraces his wife at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a famous British comic-strip character, not someone in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: The first light of day stands for a start, as in the dawn of an era.

clue.text: Secret place to store gear

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, kept hidden, as in a hidden admirer
a cupboard or small room for storing clothes and equipment

explanation.surface: A hidden spot where someone keeps their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for something concealed and a noun for a storage cupboard.

clue.text: Very large London district, you might say

indicators.note: signals that the district's name is spoken and heard as a similar-sounding word

parts.note: Wapping is a district of East London beside the Thames, once home to the newspaper presses

explanation.surface: Someone describes a part of London in casual speech.
explanation.walkthrough: WAPPING is an area of East London; said aloud it is close to the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal adjective for something huge or enormous, as in a whopper of a fish.

clue.text: Hot electrical connection for fireside feature

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
the earth wire is the grounding connection in a plug

explanation.surface: An electrician fits a hot wire near the fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: The stone floor in front of a fireplace is the feature found at the fireside.

clue.text: Good man getting lift in piece of music — it's about a book

indicators.note: the pieces before it go inside the piece of music

parts.note: a duet is a composition for two performers

indicators.note: one piece placed next to the other

parts.note: ST stands for saint, a good man
a jack lifts a car

explanation.surface: A saintly man gets a boost from a duet.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper cover wraps around a hardback, so it is literally about, meaning around, a book.

clue.text: Charge brought leader of country to stand by America in legal case

indicators.note: the letters before it are placed inside the legal case

parts.note: an action is a lawsuit brought in court

indicators.note: one piece placed directly beside the next, as people standing next to each other
the first letter of the following word heads it, as a leader heads a group

parts.note: USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A national leader is charged alongside America in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge laid against someone is a formal claim of wrongdoing, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Go touring place that's mentioned overlooking religious area

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits above the other
signals the place word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a site is a location or place
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: Somebody tours a place overlooking a diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit attractions as a tourist is to go touring.

clue.text: A gentle knock, small measure in case of emergency

parts.note: a tap is a light knock
an inch is a small unit of length

explanation.surface: A gentle knock and a tiny measurement are used in an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means if absolutely necessary, the same as when an emergency calls for it.

clue.text: Public brawl with soldiers knocked out showing a rapid descent?

indicators.note: the soldiers are removed from the brawl

parts.note: a free-for-all is an open fight anyone can join
OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers knocked out in a public brawl show a quick fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A skydiver dropping before the parachute opens makes a very rapid descent; the question mark marks the example.

clue.text: Like ecumenical event getting father in it excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A priest gets worked up about a church gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges FATHER plus IN IT; 'getting' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecumenical events bring together different Christian denominations, so they are between faiths.

clue.text: Travellers' complaint with alien creature left in car

indicators.note: the pieces before it go inside the car

parts.note: Jag is short for a Jaguar car
ET is the extraterrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: An alien is left sitting in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiredness after crossing time zones is an ailment long-haul flyers suffer.

clue.text: Staff with skill took up repeated phrase

parts.note: to man is to staff, as a post

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A team member with a talent took up a slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase chanted over and over in meditation is a repeated phrase.

clue.text: Duck to find cover in quite a lather

indicators.note: the bird takes shelter inside the run of words, signalling letters concealed within them

explanation.surface: A duck takes shelter while in a terrible state.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater dabbling bird is one species of duck.

clue.text: Dash to be seen in bar-room and participating in pub-crawl

definitions.text: Dash to be seen in bar-room and participating in pub-crawl

parts.words: Dash to be seen in bar-room and participating in pub-crawl
parts.note: the dash meant is the short line written in the compound words bar-room and pub-crawl, not a hurry between drinks

explanation.surface: Someone rushes into a pub and joins a night of bar-hopping.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a drinker dashing about; in fact the punctuation mark sits in the written words bar-room and pub-crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: The short joining line in compound words is a dash-like punctuation mark, present in both printed examples.

clue.text: Wound shown by Latin expert and judge

parts.note: an ace is a highly skilled person
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: Injury described by a classics scholar and a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to tear or cut flesh, which is what wounding does.

clue.text: Footwear young man put back behind medical institution

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium

indicators.note: the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy or young man

explanation.surface: A youth puts his shoes back at the back of a clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: An open shoe held on with straps is a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Rental property set among scattered lakes reduced to a minimum

indicators.note: the property is placed in the middle of the other letters
scattered letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: A holiday rental stands among lakes spread across the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scattered' rearranges the lakes into SKEAL, and 'set among' signals the container. In Britain a property to let is one for rent, so a let is a rental.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stripped down to its bare bones has had everything inessential removed.

clue.text: Stop learner driver wearing stetson?

indicators.note: the hat goes around the driver, as a hat is worn on the head

parts.note: a Stetson is a cowboy hat
L is the plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner motorist in a cowboy hat is told to pull over.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A command to cease moving, the same as a call to stop.

clue.text: A good neighbour's first settled in country to become sluggish

indicators.note: the pieces before it are placed inside the country

parts.note: a state is a nation or country

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A friendly neighbour moved to a new country and grew lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease flowing or developing, like still water, is to grow sluggish.
